data.narrative:
Layup Parts is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $2M+ to date. The comparable universe spans 9 private companies and 1 public entity (277810.KQ) operating in Robotics & Manufacturing, including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Two standard triangulation methods were evaluated. Stage-progression analysis, which applies a 2.5x multiplier to a base value, is not applicable: the method produces an implied valuation of $105M, more than 20x the company's total raised capital, indicating the base value proxy is unreliable. Peer-median analysis is also inapplicable due to insufficient comparable data—only 1 same-stage peer was identified within the narrow Robotics & Manufacturing set, falling short of the 3+ required for statistical confidence. Expanding to all-sector peers would introduce unacceptable measurement error.

The analysis does not support a specific valuation range at this stage. The primary constraint is data scarcity: the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage transactions to anchor relative valuation. To progress beyond this impasse, acquisition of additional seed-stage robotics comparable transactions or reliance on cost-of-capital methods would be required. Key uncertainties include runway relative to capital efficiency milestones and whether founder Zack Eakin has achieved technical de-risking milestones typical for seed advancement.
